native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I like very much pizza.”. O certo é “I like pizza very much.”. Em português dizemos “gosto muito de pizza”, mas a ordem em inglês é outra. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.

en.tip: The verb “depend” always goes with “on”, never “of”.

native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I live here since 2020.”. O certo é “I have lived here since 2020.”. Em português usamos o presente, mas o inglês pede outro tempo. Ouça o Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “have”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “I live here since”?
en.tip: With “since” we use the present perfect: “I have lived”, not “I live”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I live here since 2020.”. The right way is “I have lived here since 2020.”. Portuguese uses the present, but English needs another tense. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I bought a book in the library.
in.right: I bought a book in the bookstore.

in.answer_say: Bookstore! I buy books at the bookstore.

native.tip: “Library” é biblioteca. Livraria é “bookstore”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I bought a book in the library.”. O certo é “I bought a book in the bookstore.”. Esse falso cognato confunde muita gente. Ouça o Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “bookstore”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Library” means a place to borrow books. A shop is a “bookstore”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I bought a book in the library.”. The right way is “I bought a book in the bookstore.”. This false friend confuses many people. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I am very exciting about the trip.
in.right: I am very excited about the trip.
in.why: I feel excited. A trip is exciting.
in.answer_say: Excited! I am excited about the party.

native.tip: Para sentimentos usamos “-ed”: “excited”. Para coisas, “-ing”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I am very exciting about the trip.”. O certo é “I am very excited about the trip.”. Quem sente é “excited”; o que causa a emoção é “exciting”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “excited”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: For feelings we use “-ed”: “excited”. For things, “-ing”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I am very exciting about the trip.”. The right way is “I am very excited about the trip.”. The person who feels is “excited”; the thing that causes it is “exciting”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: My cousin is married with a doctor.
in.right: My cousin is married to a doctor.
in.answer_say: To! She is married to my brother.

native.tip: Em inglês, “casado com” é “married to”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “My cousin is married with a doctor.”. O certo é “My cousin is married to a doctor.”. O “com” do português não vira “with” aqui. Ouça o Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “to”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In English, “casado com” is “married to”.

in.wrong: I am agree with you.

native.tip: “Agree” já é verbo. Não use “am” antes dele.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I am agree with you.”. O certo é “I agree with you.”. Em português é “estou de acordo”, mas em inglês é só “agree”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “agree”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Agree” is already a verb. Do not put “am” before it.

in.hook_say: Is it has or there is?
in.wrong: It has a lot of people here.
in.right: There are a lot of people here.
in.answer_say: There are! There are many people here.

native.tip: Para dizer que existe algo, use “there is” ou “there are”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “It has a lot of people here.”. O certo é “There are a lot of people here.”. O verbo “ter” do português tem dois usos; em inglês são dois verbos. Ouça o Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “There are”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: To say that something exists, use “there is” or “there are”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “It has a lot of people here.”. The right way is “There are a lot of people here.”. The Portuguese “ter” has two uses; English uses two different verbs. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: Is cold today.
in.answer_say: It! It is hot today.

native.tip: Em inglês, a frase precisa de sujeito: “It is cold”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “Is cold today.”. O certo é “It is cold today.”. Em português dizemos “está frio”, sem sujeito. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “It”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In English, the sentence needs a subject: “It is cold”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “Is cold today.”. The right way is “It is cold today.”. In Portuguese we say “está frio” with no subject. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I go to home after work.

native.tip: Com “home”, não usamos “to”: “go home”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I go to home after work.”. O certo é “I go home after work.”. Home é uma exceção que vale decorar. Ouça o Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “go”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: With “home”, we do not use “to”: “go home”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I go to home after work.”. The right way is “I go home after work.”. Home is an exception worth remembering. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: She don't like coffee.
in.answer_say: Doesn't! He doesn't like tea.

native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “She don't like coffee.”. O certo é “She doesn't like coffee.”. É um erro muito comum, até para quem já estuda há anos. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “doesn't”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: With “he”, “she” and “it” we use “doesn't”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “She don't like coffee.”. The right way is “She doesn't like coffee.”. A very common mistake, even after years of study. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I need to make my homework.
in.right: I need to do my homework.
in.answer_say: Do! I always do my homework.

native.tip: Tarefa de casa é “do homework”. Em português usamos “fazer” para tudo.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I need to make my homework.”. O certo é “I need to do my homework.”. Em inglês, “fazer” se divide em “make” e “do”. Ouça o Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “do”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: Homework is “do homework”. In Portuguese we use “fazer” for everything.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I need to make my homework.”. The right way is “I need to do my homework.”. In English, “fazer” splits into “make” and “do”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

native.comment: Resposta: “arrive”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “when I will arrive”?
